# Establish shared project terminology

Discover and maintain the meanings that code, decisions and documents share.

[All skills](index.md) · [Collection overview](../../README.md) · [Research and inspiration](../../standards/framework-evidence.md)

## When to use it

Use when onboarding to a domain, reconciling competing terms or introducing a consequential concept.

Example request:

> Find what eligible means in this project and reconcile the code, decisions and interface wording.

Expected result: A sourced terminology record with context, accepted meanings, aliases and unresolved differences.

## A concrete example

This illustrative example starts from the source facts below.

**Source facts and constraints:** The sources use ready, approved and eligible. Their equivalence has not been established, and each may express a different condition.

**Before**

> Ready, approved and eligible all mean the account can proceed.

**After**

> Keep the three labels distinct until sources establish their meanings. Record which condition permits the account to proceed.

## Install and use

Install this skill from the versioned collection in a supported Agent Skills environment:

```sh
npx skills add https://github.com/theGeekist/skills/tree/v1.6.0 --skill establish-project-language
```

Select the intended agent and installation scope when prompted. This CLI installation is separate from ChatGPT plugin registration and mobile availability. Client discovery and activation require their own verification.

Read the [complete skill instructions](../../skills/establish-project-language/SKILL.md) and [bundled purpose reference](../../skills/establish-project-language/references/writing.md) for the full conditions and exceptions.

## Inspiration and local decisions

DDD informs context-specific meaning; SKOS informs concepts and labels; Good Docs informs terminology records. The local JSON registry is not a formal SKOS or ISO implementation.

- [DDD bounded contexts](https://martinfowler.com/bliki/BoundedContext.html)
- [W3C SKOS](https://www.w3.org/TR/skos-reference/)
- [Good Docs terminology](https://gitlab.com/tgdp/templates/-/tree/main/terminology-system)

The [source-to-guidance map](../../standards/framework-evidence.md) explains how these sources inform the skill and which decisions are local.
